messages:
Maya (oncall): PagerDuty alert 1m ago — GPU-pool-3 reported 100% allocation and queue_depth spiking. Customers seeing 429s and high latency. Paging SRE.
PagerDuty Bot: INCIDENT PAGER — GPU_POOL_EXHAUSTION triggered for env=prod region-us-west1. Severity: P1.
Maya (oncall): I'm looking at the dashboard — queue length jumped from ~50 to 1200 in 2m. Autoscale didn't add nodes. HPA shows stable pods=6, desired=6.
Sam (sre): I'm on it. Any recent deploys to inference service?
Jorge (mlinfra): No deploys in last 30m. I'm checking metrics pipeline — prometheus-adapter heartbeat is flaky in logs.
MetricsBot: prometheus-adapter: scrape_latency_millis: 18000, last_heartbeat: 00:02:34 ago
Maya (oncall): Customers: 3 reported elevated 5xx/429. Priya, can you surface a quick customer impact note for CS?
Priya (product): On it — telling CS to notify affected accounts about degraded request throughput.
Sam (sre): Dashboard: GPU usage per node at 96-100%. HPA metrics_provider=custom.metrics.k8s.io returning stale values. HPA controller log shows: "skipping scale, observed metrics older than 120s"
Maya (oncall): That explains no scale. Why are metrics stale? Jorge — what do you see upstream?
Jorge (mlinfra): Looking at prometheus-adapter pod logs: repeated timeouts to prometheus: "GET /api/v1/query?query=... 504 after 10s". Prometheus shows scrape backlog and high TSDB compaction stalls. Remote write queue clogged.
Sam (sre): If adapter can't query Prom, HPA will get old numbers. Could be Prom overloaded by a spike in scrape targets. Any recent config changes?
Jorge (mlinfra): No config changes. But I see massive scrape spikes from kube-state-metrics for gpu-exporter after a model warmup surge. Many nodes started model init churn.
Maya (oncall): Immediate mitigation options? Manual scale out? Bypass HPA? Route traffic to other region?
Sam (sre): Quick steps I can do now: 1) Temporarily increase inference deployment replicas (kubectl scale) to relieve queue. 2) Add nodes to GPU pool via autoscaler API (increase desired capacity) as a stopgap. 3) Restart prometheus-adapter to clear stale circuit. 4) If necessary, failover some traffic to us-east1.
Maya (oncall): Do step 1 & 3 now. Sam you have permissions?
Sam (sre): Doing: 
```
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/gpu-inference-deploy --replicas=12
kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deployment/prometheus-adapter
```
Sam (sre): scale command accepted, replicas -> 12. Rolling restart started for prometheus-adapter.
Jorge (mlinfra): Restart confirmed. Adapter logs show connection reestablished to Prom after restart. But Prom still has high query latency — adapter cached some last-known metrics to HPA.
MetricsBot: Adapter: last_query_time=00:00:22 ago, cached_metric_age=18s
Maya (oncall): Any change in queue/latency after the scale?
Sam (sre): Queue depth halved in 90s, token generation latency improving. 429s dropped from ~30/min to ~3/min. Customers still impacted but situation improving.
Priya (product): Notifying CS update 1: we see partial recovery, teams working on root cause, ETA unknown.
Jorge (mlinfra): Root cause trace so far: sudden burst of model cold starts led to heavy kube-state-metrics and gpu-exporter scrape activity. Prometheus overloaded -> adapter timed out -> HPA saw stale metrics and didn't scale. Autoscaler didn't kick because HPA didn't request scale.
Maya (oncall): Can we make autoscaling more resilient to adapter lag? E.g., fallback thresholds or use Kubernetes built-in metrics?
Sam (sre): Long term: add better HPA fallback (use node-level metrics or rollout predicate to allow manual emergency scale). Short term: increase HPA tolerance window and set secondary metric like queue_length from our internal metric API (less load on Prom).
Jorge (mlinfra): Also will add rate limit on kube-state-metrics and prioritize gpu-exporter sampling (lower scrape frequency for non-critical metrics).
Priya (product): Customers want a timeline. Can we estimate time to full recovery?
Sam (sre): If Prom compaction backlog clears and adapter stays healthy, HPA will re-evaluate within 1-2m. Manual scale added capacity should absorb load. Estimate 15-30m to stable.
Maya (oncall): Good. I'll remain primary oncall. Sam — handoff to Jorge in 30m if stable. Priya — keep CS looped.
Priya (product): Sending CS update 2: mitigation in progress, partial recovery. ETA 30m for stability estimate.
Jorge (mlinfra): Putting an action: adding an alert to detect adapter query 5xx or query latency > 5s sustained to avoid silent HPA gaps.
Sam (sre): Followup commands I executed: 
```
# emergency node increase (cloud autoscaler api)
cloudctl autoscaler update --pool gpu-pool-3 --min 6 --desired 10
```
Sam (sre): Increase accepted, cloud provider provisioning nodes (pending 3 new instances).
Maya (oncall): Any risk of overprovisioning cost blowup? Priya?
Priya (product): We decide to accept temporary cost for P1 availability. We'll reconcile with finance after.
MetricsBot: prometheus: remote_write_queue_len=0, tsdb_compaction_pending=0
Sam (sre): Prometheus back to normal now. Adapter query latency reduced. HPA now sees up-to-date metrics and suggested scaling to 14; HPA controller has begun new replica set rollout.
Maya (oncall): Queue depth down to baseline (10-20). No new customer 5xxs in last 5m.
Priya (product): CS update 3: service restored; root cause under investigation; timeline for postmortem forthcoming.
Maya (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated. Will open postmortem ticket and assign owners: Jorge for metrics pipeline, Sam for oncall runbook updates, Product for customer comms.
Sam (sre): Action items noted: 1) Harden adapter timeouts and add circuit-breakers. 2) Add HPA fallback metric and reduce scrape density. 3) Add runbook step: manual scale and autoprovision commands.
Jorge (mlinfra): I'll draft the postmortem and include Prometheus metric scrape tuning, kube-state-metrics rate limits, and HPA resilience changes.
Maya (oncall): Thanks all. If anything regresses ping this thread. :white_check_mark:
Priya (product): Filing customer follow-up tasks and thanking affected customers for patience.
PagerDuty Bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — GPU_POOL_EXHAUSTION (P1) closed by Maya (oncall).
Maya (oncall): postmortem ticket: PM-7891 created. Linking here when ready.
